name: nauty
desc: Automorphism groups of graphs and digraphs
why: Brendan McKay's graph automorphism and canonical labelling suite is serious combinatorics you can run at home on real graphs.

brief.what_it_is: nauty and Traces are C programs that compute the automorphism groups of graphs and digraphs, and can also produce a canonical labelling. The input is a graph or digraph, and the output is its automorphism group or a canonical form. The package bundles gtools, a suite of about fifty command-line tools (listed in the executables field) for generating graphs (geng, genbg, gentreeg and others), manipulating them (addedgeg, deledgeg, complg, linegraphg), and converting between formats. The homepage was unreachable, so this description comes from a mirror of the README-level docs at users.cecs.anu.edu.au.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no separate motivation beyond computing automorphism groups and canonical labellings. The mirror cites McKay's 1981 paper 'Practical Graph Isomorphism' as the origin of the design.
brief.how_it_works: The mirror page does not describe the search algorithm in detail. It says the current algorithms are described in McKay and Piperno, 'Practical Graph Isomorphism, II' (J. Symbolic Computation, 2013), and that Traces builds on Piperno's work on search-space contraction in canonical labelling.

commands_seen.context: Builds all nauty executables into the source directory.

brief.install_notes: Build from source with the GNU autoconf steps above. After make, the executables sit in the source directory and can be moved anywhere. 'make install' places them in standard locations. The page says to read the README before compiling. Stated platforms are Linux, macOS, WSL, and Cygwin. Some tools, especially shortg, need a POSIX-like environment with pipes, and on Windows WSL is the most recommended route. The mirror's version-history section says 2.9.0 introduced a serious dreadnaut bug, so 2.9.0 through 2.9.1rc2 should be upgraded if dreadnaut is relied on. No accounts, hardware or runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: It is a serious research-grade canonical labelling and automorphism toolkit, not a toy, and the bundled gtools include geng, which the page says generates non-isomorphic graphs very quickly. Anyone can compile it at home and run it on real graphs.
brief.status: Appears active. The mirror lists 2.9.3 as the downloadable release and points to a current beta, 2.9.4b8, with a changes file. No release or commit dates appeared on the pages I read, so the exact date is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage pallini.di.uniroma1.it was unreachable (URLError), so the entry relies on the ANU mirror, which may be out of date. Licensing is not open-source in the usual sense: the page says Traces and dretodot are copyright Adolfo Piperno, planarity.[ch] belongs to the Magma project, watercluster2.c and genposetg.c to Gunnar Brinkmann, nautycliquer to Niskanen and Östergård, parts of nauchromatic.c to Gordon Royle, and everything else to McKay, with 'minimal restrictions' in a COPYRIGHT file I did not read. The page also says 'Absolutely no guarantees or warranties' are made. Old or broken systems may not be supported. The 2.9.0 dreadnaut bug is noted above.
quotes: nauty and Traces are programs for computing automorphism groups of graphs and digraphs.
There is a suite of programs called gtools included in the nauty package. For example, geng can generate non-isomorphic graphs very quickly.
Absolutely no guarantees or warranties are made concerning the suitability, correctness, or any other aspect of this program.
